name: Optimization and Culling
text:
# Optimization and Culling
## Overview
Optimization and Culling refers to techniques that reduce the computational workload of object-order volume [splatting](#23-splatting.md) by skipping or discarding primitives that do not contribute significantly to the final image [G]. It solves the performance bottleneck of processing large numbers of splats, particularly in real-time rendering [G]. It sets itself apart from its siblings by focusing on pre-rasterization filtering (size culling) and screen-space occlusion checks ([early termination](#4675-early-termination.md)) rather than geometric approximation or hardware-specific pipeline optimizations [G].
## Shared principles
The splatting family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [G].
## Subtopics

### [Early Splat Termination](811-early-splat-termination.md)
An optimization that skips the processing of voxels when the accumulated opacity at the target screen pixels is already full, analogous to early ray termination in ray casting [G]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Splat Size Culling](2849-splat-size-culling.md) by operating on accumulated opacity rather than geometric footprint size, making it effective for opaque regions but costly for low-opacity scenes [G]. When to choose: Use for scenes with high opacity or significant occlusion where pixel coverage reaches full opacity quickly. See [Early Splat Termination](811-early-splat-termination.md).

### [Splat Size Culling](2849-splat-size-culling.md)
A staging optimization that discards primitives smaller than a defined threshold before [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) [G]. It trades visual fidelity for real-time frame rates by reducing the workload of splats and fragments generated during the rendering pipeline [G]. It differs from sibling methods like [Early Splat Termination](811-early-splat-termination.md) by operating at the data staging phase rather than during the per-pixel [compositing phase](#16578-hybrid-memory-compositing.md), allowing it to prevent expensive rasterization and memory allocation for negligible contributions entirely [G]. When to choose: Use for scenes with many small, negligible splats where performance is prioritized over fine detail. See [Splat Size Culling](2849-splat-size-culling.md).

### Splat State Encoding
Storing a 32-bit integer for each splat where each potential state (highlighted, selected, deleted) is encoded inside a single bit, serving as an [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) for transformation of selected splats [S1]. This allows the renderer to quickly check flags before loading an order of magnitude more of additional splat data [S1].

## Background
[Early Splat Termination](#811-early-splat-termination.md) and [Splat Size Culling](#2849-splat-size-culling.md) are standard optimizations within the splatting family for improving rendering throughput [G]. Splat State Encoding originates from the Splatshop framework for efficiently editing large Gaussian Splat models [S1].
## Sources
[S1] Splatshop: Efficiently Editing Large Gaussian Splat Models, https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.70214, fetched 2026-10-31
